rows.text: Ultima is not merely an evasive land-hosing attacker; it is a mana doubler in the command zone. Its static ability adds an additional {C} whenever you tap a land for {C}. Because every single land in this pure colorless ninety-nine produces colorless mana, resolving Ultima turns five lands into ten mana, allowing you to cast colossal Eldrazi titans, activate Planar Bridge, or execute infinite mana finishes turns ahead of normal timing. Meanwhile, Ultima's attack trigger permanently neutralizes opponents' most threatening utility lands (Cabal Coffers, Gaea's Cradle, Nykthos) and color-fixing by converting them into colorless-only Wastes.

Bracket 3: the Game Changer cap is three, filled by Ancient Tomb, Mishra's Workshop, and The One Ring. No mass land denial. Infinite mana combos (Basalt Monolith + Forsaken Monument / Rings of Brighthearth into Walking Ballista) wait until turn 6 under house rules.

rows.name: Ultima, Origin of Oblivion
rows.text: a 4/4 flying God that doubles the mana of all your lands whenever tapped for {C}, and attacks to put a blight counter on target land, permanently stripping all types and abilities to make it a colorless mana tap.

rows.name: Candelabra of Tawnos
rows.text: pay {X} and tap to untap X target lands. Because Ultima causes each land to produce two mana, untapping your lands generates massive net mana bursts.

rows.name: Deserted Temple
rows.text: pays {1} and taps to untap target land, untapping a high-yield land like Ancient Tomb, Eldrazi Temple, or Shrine of the Forsaken Gods for extra mana.

rows.name: Forsaken Monument
rows.text: adds an additional {C} whenever you tap ANY permanent for {C}, stacking with Ultima to turn ordinary lands into triple-mana powerhouses while buffing colorless creatures by +2/+2.

rows.name: Omnath, Locus of the Void
rows.text: colorless creature whose unspent mana never empties across phases and turns, turning your massive mana surpluses into floating reserves and growing Omnath into a lethal beatdown threat.

rows.name: Thespian's Stage + The Mycosynth Gardens
rows.text: copy key utility lands or artifacts on the battlefield.

rows.name: Basalt Monolith + Forsaken Monument
rows.text: Forsaken Monument adds an extra {C} when Basalt taps for {C}{C}{C}, netting 4 mana; pay {3} to untap Basalt, netting infinite colorless mana

rows.name: Basalt Monolith + Rings of Brighthearth
rows.text: tap Basalt Monolith for {C}{C}{C}, pay {3} to activate its untap ability, pay {2} to Rings of Brighthearth to copy the untap; tap Basalt between untap resolutions to net infinite colorless mana

rows.name: Basalt Monolith + Forsaken Monument + Walking Ballista
rows.text: infinite colorless mana into Walking Ballista shoots the entire table for lethal direct damage

rows.name: Mystic Forge + Sensei's Divining Top + Foundry Inspector
rows.text: with Foundry Inspector discounting artifacts by {1}, cast Sensei's Divining Top from the top of your library for free via Mystic Forge, tap Top to draw a card, and repeat to draw your entire library

rows.name: Planar Bridge
rows.text: an eight-mana artifact that pays {8} and taps to search ANY permanent card from your library directly onto the battlefield, easily funded by Ultima or infinite mana
Under Bracket 3 rules, infinite mana and Ballista kills must wait until turn 6 or later. Spend turns 1 through 5 establishing your manabase, casting Ultima, and dropping mid-game ramp engines.

guide.title: The Eldrazi titans and colossal threats

Look for an opening hand with two to three lands, early mana acceleration (Sol Ring, Mox Opal, Everflowing Chalice, Mind Stone, Expedition Map), and a card draw or mid-game ramp piece (The One Ring, Chimil, Worn Powerstone).
Turn 1-2: Deploy fast mana rocks and utility lands. Use Expedition Map to find Ancient Tomb, Mishra's Workshop, or Urza lands.
Turn 3-4: Cast Ultima, Origin of Oblivion on turn 3 or 4. Once Ultima resolves, your lands immediately produce double mana.

Turn 5: Attack with Ultima to put a blight counter on an opponent's most dangerous land (Cabal Coffers, Cradle, or a triome). Use your doubled mana pool (ten or more mana) to drop an Eldrazi titan (Ulamog, Kozilek, Sire of Seven Deaths) or an engine (Echoes of Eternity, Darksteel Monolith, Portal to Phyrexia).

Turn 6+: Under Bracket 3 rules, tutor or deploy Basalt Monolith + Forsaken Monument/Rings to generate infinite colorless mana into Walking Ballista, or wipe opposing boards with All Is Dust and overwhelm the table with annihilator attacks.
